title: Primate Phylogeny
goal: A practitioner can visually assess the Primate Phylogeny scenario using its published diagram convention.

rubric.must: A rooted branching tree visibly shows the stated sister taxa and their clade relationships.
Horizontal branch lengths visibly vary to encode the supplied evolutionary distances.
The named taxa are legible at the tree tips.
The named clade is visibly highlighted distinctly from the rest of the tree.
A visible scale or distance label identifies the evolutionary-distance interpretation.

ideal.notes: Drafted by Codex from the source, the rubric and the phylo/rectangular exemplar, without seeing the engine's own output.

review.evidence: The drawing clearly presents the supplied rectangular phylogram: Human and Chimpanzee are sister taxa, Gorilla joins their highlighted Homininae clade, followed by Orangutan and then Gibbon. Horizontal branch lengths visibly vary, all five tip labels are legible, and a 0.01 substitutions/site scale is shown.

items.evidence: The rooted tree visibly shows Human and Chimpanzee sharing an immediate ancestor, that pair joining Gorilla, then Orangutan, with Gibbon as the outermost split.
Horizontal segments have visibly different lengths consistent with a phylogram, including short terminal Human/Chimpanzee branches and longer basal branches.
Human, Chimpanzee, Gorilla, Orangutan, and Gibbon are all clearly legible beside their respective tips.
Human, Chimpanzee, and Gorilla are distinctly emphasized with blue branches, a pale blue region, a bracket, and the label Homininae.
A visible scale bar is labeled 0.01 substitutions/site, and accompanying text identifies horizontal distance as substitutions/site.
